question: Should pending Skill Workshop approvals always bind apply, reject, and quarantine to the reviewed proposal version and require a fresh review after any revision?
rationale: The implementation intentionally introduces an operator-visible fail-closed behavior for a new approval flow; code review can establish its mechanics, but maintainers must choose whether that stricter lifecycle contract is the desired product policy.

options.title: Adopt reviewed-version binding
options.body: Accept the fail-closed approval contract so an approval can never act on proposal content changed after the operator reviewed it.

options.title: Keep approvals Proposal-ID-only
options.body: Preserve the current approval behavior and limit version binding to an explicit opt-in flow if avoiding a retry after revisions is more important than snapshot integrity.

recommendation.title: Adopt reviewed-version binding
recommendation.body: Accept the fail-closed approval contract so an approval can never act on proposal content changed after the operator reviewed it.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged approval-policy work is the closest established ownership signal for the resolver contract this PR extends.
